reason: The cited evidence shows that high-entropy alloys can be superconductors (E1) and that mixing entropy can improve low-temperature critical current (E2) or robustness (E3), but none of the passages provides direct support for the key premises that increasing configurational entropy enhances electron–phonon coupling, induces favorable local disorder, or raises Tc in bcc alloys. The claims about the mechanism and optimal window are entirely unsupported by the cited texts.
premises: Increasing configurational entropy enhances electron–phonon coupling
Increasing configurational entropy induces favorable local structural disorder
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling and local disorder increase Tc
The effect is bounded by an optimal compositional window
The mechanism applies to bcc high-entropy alloys
